I want to make a SaaS like "Workable" I need a team of Devs or a Full Stack dev to help me plan the requirements and begin making the SaaS. Budget is not final and no time wasters please. https://www.workable.com/
</job>

text:
Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne, a full stack developer with 7 years of experience building modern web apps with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS.

Your Workable-style SaaS is the kind of project I’d approach carefully from the start: first by helping define the product requirements, core workflows, and MVP scope, then by turning that plan into a clean, scalable build. For a platform like this, I’d focus on the essentials that matter most early on — user onboarding, account and team management, job and candidate workflows, dashboards, and the underlying API structure needed to support the product as it grows.

I also understand the importance of avoiding wasted effort. Before writing much code, I’d want to help map out the system clearly so the first version is built around the right priorities. That usually means identifying what needs to be in the initial release, what can wait, and how to structure the app so future features can be added without rework.

One project that reflects my approach is a home goods storefront rebuild for Juniper & Ash Home. I replaced a slow theme-based shop with a headless storefront and CMS the marketing team could edit themselves. The result was a reduction in largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.3s, and organic traffic increased by 38% in 3 months. That project reinforced how important it is to build for both performance and maintainability from day one.

If you’re looking for someone who can help shape the requirements and begin building the foundation of the SaaS, I’d be glad to help. I can work with you to define the MVP, identify the right technical architecture, and start implementing the first version in a way that supports future expansion.

If you’d like, I can help you break the product into phases and outline what the initial build should include.
